AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: On keeping / cover
text: THE PIECE. THE CHANGE. THE NEXT CHAPTER.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Inside cover / an honest premise
text: A REPAIR BEGINS WITH A PERSON.
Not every piece has a grand story. Sometimes it is simply the shirt that fits, the jacket you borrow or the jeans you already know.
This guide helps you describe a change without needing the technical name. The actual garment and a repairer determine what is possible.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Contents / a guide in four parts
text: Finish, repair type and a clear request.
Records, care information and return visits.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Opening / keep the good part
text: The familiar weight. The right sleeve. The way it falls. Start with what you want to keep.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Opening / a detail is enough
text: A considered repair protects what matters while making the change understandable. Illustrative garment, not a documented repair result.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Material study / a closer look
text: A CLOSER LOOK / ILLUSTRATIVE DARNING STUDY

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Material study / what the cloth decides
text: A photo can explain where the problem is. It cannot confirm the strength of the surrounding cloth, the feel of the repair or the best method.
The studio needs your observation, not an expert conclusion.
“Not sure” is a useful answer about fibre, method or finish.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Finish / closest practical match
text: Let attention stay on the piece.
A close colour match and familiar construction can reduce the contrast of a repair. It may still be visible, and the material may feel different.
What is the closest practical match? What will still be visible? Could the finish affect how the piece falls?

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Finish / deliberate contrast
text: A contrasting thread, patch or fastening can make the repair part of the piece. The colour is a preference; suitability still depends on the garment.
Ask to see a sample. A beautiful contrast still needs a practical method.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Taxonomy / useful codes
text: A CODE HELPS THE STUDIO. WORDS HELP YOU.
The code is an index, not a diagnosis. The description stays next to it on the screen, tag and work ticket.
Not sure which kind? Begin with Q01: an assessment.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Taxonomy / repair index
text: Fabric is thin or has opened up.
Two pieces of cloth are separating.
A zip that will not work
The pull, teeth or slider needs attention.
A fastening needs a closer look.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Request / three details
text: Use a name you will recognise: “My everyday shirt” is enough.
Elbow, seam, fastening or edge. Say “Not sure” when needed.
Close match, visible contrast or advice before choosing.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Request / paper and screen
text: BRING THE DETAILS INTO THE CONVERSATION.
The prototype prints saved details. Local requests have no public QR. This brief is not permission to begin work.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Agreement / requested intention
text: A close match at the elbow.
Keep attention on the original garment.
The area you can see, before assessment.
Not confirmed by describing a repair.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Agreement / assessed proposal
text: A small visible difference may remain.
A wider reinforcement may be needed.
Review the complete proposal before deciding.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Decision / a useful pause
text: UNCERTAINTY IS A REASON TO ASK.
A request describes the intention. A proposal explains the practical limits. The decision belongs after the comparison.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Decision / three paths
text: Review the whole proposal, then record a decision.
Keep the proposal pending while the question is resolved.
Review the new scope. An earlier approval is not carried forward.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Record / a stable reference
text: A stable reference travels with the piece. A repair code describes the type; a revision number describes a changing proposal. They are different kinds of information.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Record / paper to digital
text: The everyday shirt. An illustrative garment record.
The sample record opens from its printed tag or typed ID. A new repair request can begin with these garment details without changing the old record.
Preview QR requires access to the portfolio. Repoint and scan-test before public printing.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Care / a boundary worth keeping
text: The repair record adds context. It does not replace garment-specific care instructions, confirm an unknown fibre content or create new wash symbols.
The garment ID and the documented repair description.
The original label and any repair-specific advice from the repairer.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Follow-up / something changed
text: Keep the record and describe the place that needs attention. A new request starts a fresh assessment; it does not rewrite the earlier repair.
Uncertainty is welcome at every stage.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: At a glance / a useful checklist
text: We are talking about the same garment and location.
I understand the proposed finish and scope.
Price and timing have been explained.
I know how to ask a question or review a revision.

AFTERFORM-On-Keeping-Second-Edition.pdf.title: Colophon / production and evidence
text: 170 × 240 mm. Twenty-four pages. Proposed saddle stitch. Six folded sheets. Pages are supplied in reading order; the printer performs imposition after paper and binding are confirmed.
Proposed stock: uncoated 120 gsm text with a 200 gsm cover. Check grain, creep, gutter and colour on a physical proof. This RGB PDF is not a press-certified file.
Concept and implementation: Jocelyn Martinez, with AI assistance. Bodoni Moda, Karla and Inconsolata are used under the SIL Open Font License. Material images are original generated illustrations.
No operating studio, customer research, repair results or environmental savings are claimed.

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Identity standards / cover
text: A SYSTEM FOR PRINT, PRODUCT AND THE STUDIO.

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Concept / design grammar
text: A named garment anchors the story. One visible intervention expresses the repair. A practical information rail carries the ID, repair type and next action. Quiet space separates the emotional invitation from operational detail.

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Identity / clear space
text: 03 / CLEAR SPACE IS PART OF THE MARK
x = lowercase height. Minimum clear space = 0.5x.
Measure from the visible outline, not the exported SVG bounds. Keep rules, copy and die cuts outside that space.

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Identity / optical adaptation
text: WORDMARK / 144 px digital or 35 mm print minimum target

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Identity / correct and incorrect use
text: Use supplied outlines. Never distort width, add an outline or shadow, fill letters with a photo, or rearrange the word into a new symbol. The wordmark is a licensed type-based design, not custom lettering.

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Colour / behaviour
text: Use vermilion for one emphasis. It is not the only status signal. Avoid normal-size vermilion copy on lilac (3.43:1). Keep essential reading on the quiet combination (13.32:1).

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Typography / five useful scales
text: Display / Bodoni Moda, optical sizing on
Describe the place that needs attention.
Body: Karla 17/27 px. Label: Karla 14/20 px. Code: Inconsolata 13/18 px.
Print body: 11/16 pt. Essential tag text: 9/12 pt minimum target.

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Graphic language / not decoration
text: Identity, classification and version are separate. Never use the repair code as a garment ID.

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Labels / anatomy
text: Stable ID and recognisable garment name.
Plain-language problem, then the repair code.
Review, ask, approve a version, or collect.
Add a status word, never colour alone. Keep personal data off exterior labels.

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Grid / shared rhythm, different layouts
text: 4 px UI base. 6 mm editorial rhythm. Equal margins are a choice, not a law.

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Image system / material before spectacle
text: 11 / SHOW THE PIECE, THEN THE DETAIL
Soft side light. Realistic material scale. One legible intervention. No invented hands, tools or documentary claims.
Generated illustration is labelled. Exact copy lives in authored flat artwork.

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Interface / status grammar
text: 12 / A STATUS SHOULD SAY WHAT HAPPENS NEXT
A new revision needs a fresh decision.
Show the version; allow reversal in the prototype.
A digital example approval never authorises a real-world repair.

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Motion / explicit and quiet
text:
160 ms: colour and border feedback.
280 ms: a joining-rule reveal.
No delay before form feedback.
No automatic cinematic entrance.
Brand demonstration: user-triggered, one pass, then a still frame. Reduced motion displays the result immediately.

AFTERFORM-Identity-Standards.pdf.title: Production / practical boundaries
text: PDFs use RGB colours with embedded type. Confirm the printer, substrate and profile before separation. Do not invent a Pantone match. Supply 3 mm bleed when required; keep essential text 5 mm from trim and holes.
Print tags at actual size. Test glare, reading distance, hole placement and QR scanning. Packaging nets are dimensioned prototypes, not supplier-approved cutting dies.
